After consuming three glassfuls of home-brewed cordial at Grey Shutters, Isolde becomes dizzy, giggles, falls asleep, and develops a severe headache. Her mother assumes Nell deliberately got Isolde drunk and forbids Isolde from playing or speaking with Nell. Isolde secretly meets Nell near the Nymph's Well to bid her a tearful farewell, giving her a lock of her hair, and later sends her a note and a tissue-paper bookmark at school. After Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup, Mrs. Pembroke realizes her mistake and restores their friendship. Isolde attends a concert with Nell and hosts her great-aunt Lavinia Pembroke, who funds Isolde's music lessons after Nell intercedes on her behalf. Over the years, Isolde and Nell attend Brierley school together, craft stories for a writing club, and travel to town for a fair with her father and Miss Lavinia Pembroke. unit: Residing at Grey Shutters in Brierley with her quiet brother Obed, Thirza agreed to adopt a young boy from a Nova Scotian orphanage to help on their farm. When Obed accidentally brought home a young girl named Nell Harcourt due to a mix-up, Thirza initially insisted on returning her. However, out of compassion and Obed's quiet desire, Thirza decided to keep Nell and take charge of her upbringing. unit: Isolde Pembroke returns home to Pear Hill after visiting her aunt in Delford and soon meets Nell Harcourt, who visits with Thirza Abernethy. The two girls quickly become bosom friends, swearing a solemn vow over a pretend stream to remain loyal friends forever. Together they share books, play around Pear Hill and the surrounding woods, and create a playhouse named Larkrise. After consuming three glassfuls of home-brewed cordial at Grey Shutters, Isolde becomes dizzy, giggles, falls asleep, and develops a severe headache. Her mother assumes Nell deliberately got Isolde drunk and forbids Isolde from playing or speaking with Nell. Isolde secretly meets Nell near the Nymph's Well to bid her a tearful farewell, giving her a lock of her hair, and later sends her a note and a tissue-paper bookmark at school. After Nell saves Isolde's younger sister Posy Fay from croup, Mrs. Pembroke realizes her mistake and restores their friendship. Isolde attends a concert with Nell and hosts her great-aunt Lavinia Pembroke, who funds Isolde's music lessons after Nell intercedes on her behalf. Over the years, Isolde and Nell attend Brierley school together, craft stories for a writing club, and travel to town for a fair with her father and Miss Lavinia Pembroke. When Nell attends Regent's class while Isolde does not, and later when Nell goes away to the Academy, the two remain loyal companions.
